chunks: As for what was narrated by Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad, from Abū Jaʿfar, from Abū al-Jawzāʾ, from al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿUlwān, from ʿAmr ibn Khālid, from Zayd, from his forefathers, from ʿAlī عليه السلام, who said:

The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: “If the martyr dies on the same day or on the next day, then bury him in his clothes; but if he remains for days until his wound changes, he is to be given ghusl (ritual bath).”

So this report accords with the ʿĀmmah, and we do not act upon it, because we have explained that when one slain does not die in the battlefield, his ghusl becomes obligatory whether his condition has changed or has not changed. The practice should be according to that, if Allah the Exalted wills.

Al-Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, said: As for one afflicted with smallpox, one who is burned, and others like them whose skin, limbs, and flesh have been broken down by afflictions, if touching them by hand during their washing would remove some of their flesh or hair, then they are not to be touched by hand, and water is to be poured over them.

But if it is feared that the water would cause some of their skin or hair to fall away, then water is not to be brought near them, and tayammum is to be performed for them with earth, just as tayammum is performed for a living person incapacitated by chronic illness when he needs tayammum due to janabah. Thus his face is wiped from the hairline of his head to the tip of his nose, and the outer side of his two hands is wiped.

key_terms.التَّيَمُّمِ: dry ablution performed when water cannot be used
key_terms.التُّرَابِ: earth or dust used for tayammum
key_terms.الشَّهِيدُ: the martyr; one killed in a qualifying cause whose burial rulings are discussed here
key_terms.الْمَجْدُورُ: the person afflicted with smallpox or similar bodily deterioration
key_terms.الْمَعْرَكَةِ: the battlefield; the place whose circumstance affects the ruling on the slain
key_terms.الْمُحْتَرِقُ: the burned person whose body may be too fragile for direct washing
key_terms.جَنَابَتِهِ: the state of major ritual impurity requiring purification
key_terms.غُسِّلَ: was given ghusl (ritual washing) for burial preparation

ai.seo_question: When should a martyr be buried without ghusl, and when is tayammum performed for the deceased instead of washing?
ai.summary: This passage discusses legal rulings concerning the washing and burial of the martyr and of deceased persons whose bodies are severely damaged. It also records the compiler's rejection of one report in favor of the established ruling that a slain person who does not die in the battlefield must be given ghusl, and it explains when tayammum is performed for the deceased instead of washing.
